PullRequest.Title: agentHost: avoid duplicate discovered plugins
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Explicitly configured host plugins and client-synced plugins now shadow automatic discovery of the same plugin ID.

A plugin such as `azure-exp` could appear twice in a session: once from client sync and once from SDK discovery of its original installation. The parent IDs matched, but the MCP children referred to different paths. This made the MCP UI's name matching ambiguous, leaving the plugin card without runtime status or Start/Stop controls and displaying additional server rows.

The fix suppresses only the redundant discovered plugin. Explicit loading, error, and disabled states remain authoritative; removing the explicit contribution restores discovery. Different plugins with the same name remain distinct. No changes to UI matching or SDK plugin registration.

## Tests

- Regression coverage for client and host precedence, loading/error/enabled/disabled states, synchronized MCP child identities, same-named distinct plugins, and removal fallback.
- Verified both new regression tests fail without the shadowing guard and pass with it.
- 120 targeted tests passed on the new main-based branch across Copilot customization, discovery, MCP runtime, and MCP UI suites.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- Targeted ESLint and pre-commit hygiene passed.
- Manually verified in the OSS customizations UI by the reporter.

This branch is based directly on main and does not include the pending MCP-start changes in #337370.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold or warm session customization retrieval for slash-command completion and session UI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: getChatCustomizations awaits host/client synchronization, initial discovered-customization settlement, and MCP discovery refresh before resolving and returning the published list. The changed code then builds an in-memory Set and filters discovered plugins; that work is on the critical path but does not add an asynchronous boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover and parse workspace/user customizations and plugin manifests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lazy discovery entry per active session/workspace anchor, refreshed after debounced discovery changes; plugin-root filesystem probes and parsing scale with discovered plugin files and roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery, manifest reads, and parsing already completed before _resolveCustomizationEnablement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold retrieval waits for the initial settled discovery; warm retrieval reuses the current discovered snapshot unless a watched source changed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SDK customization discovery through the Copilot client
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Grouped discovery calls for the session's configured roots, not one new call per explicit plugin ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical SDK discovery occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold retrieval waits for SDK discovery; the added Set/filter executes only after results are materialized.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One refresh invocation per settled retrieval, with definitions grouped by workspace discovery state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same refresh was awaited before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the customization snapshot is returned.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Host customizations plus the URI-deduplicated union of active-client customizations, followed by discovered customizations. The new Set construction and membership checks are O(H+C+D) with effective cardinality after client URI deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Host syncs, all active-client syncs, discovered-entry settlement, and MCP refresh are awaited with Promise.all; the changed synchronous filter adds no concurrency or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SessionDiscoveredEntry is lazily created and retains its current snapshot; refreshes are debounced and canceled/coalesced. Host and per-client sync promises are retained. The new Set is ephemeral per resolution and introduces no cache or retained state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: direct call-path inspection shows no new boundary and only bounded linear in-memory work over lists that were already traversed and projected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact plugin counts vary, but customization lists are configuration-sized and the only new cost is one transient Set plus linear membership checks; no evidence supports user-visible latency or GC pressure.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff suppresses duplicate discovered plugins without increasing boundary count, critical-path waits, or asymptotic complexity.

Scenarios.Scenario: Client plugin sync, loading/status updates, removal, and discovery-change publication
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A changed client contribution or debounced discovery refresh constructs a SessionCustomizationsChanged/Updated action synchronously before the event is forwarded to session progress consumers. _resolveCustomizationEnablement now builds the explicit-ID Set before projection and publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize and parse client plugins during syncCustomizations and resolveSyncedCustomization
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One plugin-manager sync per genuinely changed client slice; unchanged re-subscriptions are skipped, and client syncs are serialized per client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Client plugin materialization/parsing and per-client serialization already occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The loading action may publish before completion; settled updates follow parsing. The changed deduplication executes during action construction only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward session customization actions through the agent progress stream
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reset action per changed sync/removal/discovery refresh plus per-item status updates already emitted by the existing sync flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same events were forwarded, with duplicate discovered plugins included.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Action payload construction is synchronous; the diff can reduce payload cardinality by omitting a shadowed discovered plugin and does not add emissions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active clients and each client's URI-deduplicated customizations, plus discovered customizations. Set work is linear per existing publish event; event frequency is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sync work is chained per client via the previous sync promise; independent client states may settle concurrently. Discovery refreshes are delayed/coalesced. The diff creates no burst or additional scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Identical client input is recognized and skips re-sync/publication; discovery state is retained and debounced. The explicit-ID Set is short-lived and does not accumulate across events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: all publication sites call the same resolver, and changed lines neither increase publication frequency nor invoke plugin sync/discovery.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Status-heavy syncs can invoke resolution multiple times, but each invocation covers configuration-sized collections and replaces duplicate output with a membership check; there is no realistic evidence of jank or throughput loss.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added CPU/allocation is bounded linear bookkeeping and duplicate suppression reduces downstream payload/work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session launch snapshot and restart-reason evaluation through getAppliedPlugins
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Snapshot construction awaits enablement initialization, host/client syncs, discovered settlement, and MCP refresh, then resolves customization enablement and builds parsed plugin configuration before launch/restart comparison.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Host/client plugin parsing and discovered customization settlement
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Grouped host sync, one pending sync per active client, and one session discovery entry; no calls are added per ID lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All parsing and discovery waits were already on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the launch snapshot can progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One refresh invocation for the session snapshot, unchanged by explicit plugin count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited in the existing Promise.all before configuration assembly.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled explicit plugins, discovered directories/plugins, MCP definitions, and active clients. The added Set/filter remains O(H+C+D), while parsed-plugin assembly already scales over these lists and children.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing host, client, discovery, and MCP operations execute concurrently under Promise.all; per-client sync ordering remains serialized. No new subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pending sync promises and discovered snapshots are reused; no new persistent cache. Duplicate discovered plugin containers are filtered from enablement resolution but discovery itself remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from direct inspection of getAppliedPlugins and resolver call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large plugin configurations increase linear in-memory work, but the PR removes a duplicate from resolved maps/output and does not amplify expensive operations; measurable degradation is unlikely.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression and no separately proven shipped performance-regression fix: the PR addresses duplicate identity/UI behavior, while expensive discovery work still occurs unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced customization retrieval, sync/publication, discovery refresh, and session snapshot paths. The production change adds one ephemeral Set and linear membership filtering over already-materialized configuration-sized collections, with no new filesystem, SDK/IPC, network, subprocess, serialization fan-out, concurrency burst, cache retention, or lifecycle cost. Test-only service setup and regression cases do not affect production performance. No valid performance findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
